subject: Clarification on which artifacts Redwood persists by default & deletion steps
messages:
From: Priyanka Rao <pri@acme-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Which items do you persist by default (requests/responses, prompts, outputs)?

Hi Logan,

Hope you’re well. Our security team is doing a final pass on data flows for the checkout assistant POC. They asked a few granular questions I couldn’t answer from the public docs:

- Which artifacts does Redwood store by default (original request, model tokens, model outputs, derived embeddings, evals)?
- Are prompts and temporary prefixes treated differently from final generated outputs?
- What are the default retention periods and how can we trigger a full purge on demand?

We’re evaluating whether the hosted flow meets our audit window. Can you confirm the defaults and any self-serve deletion paths (console or API)? If it’s easier, happy to schedule a 20 min call.

Thanks,
Priyanka Rao
Product Security Lead, Acme Retail
pri@acme-retail.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <pri@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, payments@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Which items do you persist by default (requests/responses, prompts, outputs)?

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary first, then operational details and where to find the controls.

Summary (defaults for Hosted API):
- Requests & model responses (request metadata + tokens): retained by default for 30 days.
- Prompts / prefix contexts (short-term caches): by default held in ephemeral cache for up to 3 days; not archived unless you opt into the "logging" telemetry setting.
- Final generated outputs (if flagged by your app as "save_output"): treated as customer artifacts and retained 365 days by default; otherwise they follow the request/response 30-day TTL.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, index vectors): persisted by default if you call the embeddings API; retention depends on the storage class — standard embeddings retention is 365 days unless you set a different TTL in the Console.
- Evals and quality metrics: stored by default for 180 days; you can change eval retention per-project.

Operational details:
- Self-serve deletion: Console -> Project -> Data -> Logs allows scoped deletes (by date, route, or request-id). For bulk or programmatic deletes use the admin API: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/data/delete with a deletion spec (support will provide an example).
- Full account purges: we require a verified request (signed ATO contact + order id). For Hosted customers we can execute a full purge within 72 hours after verification — this is a manual process initiated by Support for auditability.
- Private/Dedicated: customers managing Redwood Private can override all defaults via their control plane; retention is configurable in the deployment manifest.

Notes on what counts as a "log":
- "Request" = request headers, metadata (client IP if enabled), full input prompt payload.
- "Response" = token-level output, streaming deltas, and final text.
- "Prompt derivatives" = embeddings, eval records, and any generated artifacts saved by the app.

Attachment: I’m attaching our internal retention matrix so you can map scenarios to TTLs.
[attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

If you want, I can set up a short call with our security PM (Marissa) to walk through the verification and purge runbook.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <pri@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, payments@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Which items do you persist by default (requests/responses, prompts, outputs)? — additional clarifications

Priyanka — adding a couple of points from the product/controls side:

1) Default retention is a per-project config in Hosted; the defaults Logan listed are the out-of-the-box values, but we can change them for enterprise customers under an MSA.

2) Deletion semantics: our delete endpoint issues a tombstone marker for the indexed artifacts and schedules physical removal per the storage backend (typically within 7–30 days depending on tier). Note that cached KV entries for model prefixes may persist a short interval for performance; those are treated as ephemeral and not included in audit logs unless logging is enabled.

3) Audit trail: any support-assisted purge generates an immutable audit record (who initiated, what scope, related ticket). That record is retained separately for compliance purposes — we do not surface the raw payload in the audit record.

4) GDPR / EU residency: for customers using EU regions, data residency policies apply; the retention controls are the same but deletion operations are executed within the region.

Action items for Acme Retail (recommended):
- Review retention_matrix_v2.xlsx and mark any non-defaults you want applied.
- If you require an immediate account-level purge, please open a Support ticket with the ATO contact and a signed request. We will triage and provide the manual purge ETA.

Happy to hop on a call next week to walk your security team through the console UI.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks Logan and Marissa — that helps a lot. I shared the matrix with our security ops and they’ve flagged two items we want tightened (prompts retained in telemetry; embeddings retention). I’ll open the support ticket today with the ATO contact and requested scope.

Can you pls propose 30-min windows next week for a short walkthrough of: console delete UI, the admin delete API example, and the support purge runbook? Prefer Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Best,
Priyanka
